A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TaoAvatar and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Matching sections, equations, four tables, and seventeen figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original avatar reconstruction and animation experiments, rendering-speed measurements, and component ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–4 and qualitative appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same SMPLX++ representation, StyleUnet teacher, deformation baking into an MLP student, and position/color blend shapes. Diagram revisions do not establish an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions use TalkBody4D, four ActorHQ sequences, two dancing sequences, and two exaggerated-expression sequences. The reconstruction, novel-view, gesture/expression animation, and device demonstrations retain the same coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding tables and qualitative comparisons retain GaussianAvatar, 3DGS-Avatar, MeshAvatar, and AnimatableGS, alongside the teacher/student variants. Changed citation numbers do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Both retain the 1500 × 2000 evaluation resolution, common SMPLX representation, image and geometry metrics, training budgets, and RTX4090 speed-testing conditions. Appendix masking, face-cropping, and mobile animation/rendering settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and the appendices retain the same template, mesh/Gaussian deformation, teacher-baking, normal-loss, and semantic-loss analyses. The illustrated failure cases are unchanged; appendix reflow does not add or remove an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values and rankings. For example, Table 1 reports student novel-view PSNR 33.81 and 156 FPS in both versions. Figure 15 scores and the matched qualitative examples also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), including coordinate transformations, loss definitions, blend-shape operations, and the appendix body/cloth deformation decomposition, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about high-fidelity lightweight avatars, teacher-student deformation baking, TalkBody4D, and real-time stereo rendering on Apple Vision Pro. Contribution scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the teacher-versus-student detail interpretation, approximate-relighting caveat, online latent-code compromise, and limitations involving loose clothing and inaccurate SMPLX alignment. Appendix D moves partly onto an earlier page without changing its discussion.

D1.justification: Figure 1 replaces the explicit Unity identification with the generic label Rendering Engine, removing deployment specificity without establishing an engine change. Hyperparameters, quantization/interpolation details, project access information, and the planned dataset release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes Feng et al., Learning Disentangled Avatars with Hybrid 3D Representations, from Section 2 and the bibliography (v1 reference 15). The remaining literature coverage and substantive research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Main and appendix prose and section order remain essentially unchanged. Small edits affect headers, citation numbering, and diagram terminology, including BS Coefficient becoming Facial BS Coefficient in Figure 13.

P2.justification: Several figures use higher-resolution image assets. Figure 1 changes its engine label, and Figure 13 is compacted, rearranged, and given model citations, producing minor appendix reflow. The same seventeen figures and four tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Sharper figures provide modest presentation gains, but Figure 13 introduces incorrect citations: Qwen2.5-3B points to Dressing Avatars [58], and Bert-vits2 points to HUGS [29]. Figure 1 also removes Unity identification. These localized losses in documentation accuracy and specificity slightly outweigh the visual refinements; the scientific method and evidence remain unchanged.
